chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mufaddal ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said to me: 'O Mufaddal! Whoever exposes himself to a tyrannical ruler and a calamity befalls him, he will not be rewarded for it, nor will he be granted patience for it.'

key_terms.سُلْطَانٍ جَائِرٍ: Tyrannical ruler or just ruler who acts unjustly

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of exposing oneself to a tyrannical ruler according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of the era of political quietism, this hadith clarifies that suffering under a tyrant is not automatically a merit-worthy trial unless it stems from sincere *Amr bil-Ma'ruf* (commanding good). It warns that mere exposure to the ruler's oppression, without the specific intent of religious duty, results in a loss of both reward (*ajr*) and the spiritual virtue of patience (*sabr*), highlighting the Shia emphasis on intentionality in political engagement.
